10.1002_aenm.202505228: For anode‐free sodium batteries to achieve practical consideration, highly reversible chemistries require exceptional ≥99.95% coulombic efficiencies that maintain over prolonged cycling periods. To do so, consumption of this severely limited sodium inventory must be restricted while metal nucleation processes that comprise the in situ formed metal anode are improved. Herein, we describe a fluorine‐free carborane electrolyte that satisfies these criteria by emphasizing reductive stability and weakly coordinating anion behavior as design principles. We find this approach promotes the development of a thin, robust SEI chemistry rich in both organic speciation and boron. The electrolyte described herein exhibits ideal metal nucleation behavior on one‐micron thin carbonaceous current collector surfaces and achieves a metal deposition/stripping efficiency near parity for 400 cycles. This novel anode chemistry is introduced to anode‐free full cell configurations where 87% of the initial discharge capacity is retained after 1000 cycles at 2.0 C. Post‐test characterization of deep‐cycled anode‐free cells reveals suppressed capacity fade in these systems is attributed to the chemical stability of the carborane anion.
10.1002_aenm.71695: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries promise large‐scale storage, yet anode irreversibility remains the principal barrier. Eutectic electrolytes, comprising hydrogen‐bond donors (HBDs) and acceptors (HBAs), can suppress H 2 O activity and regulate Zn 2+ desolvation through hydrogen‐bond networks, offering a promising remedy. However, the screening of polyol‐based HBDs still relies on empirical trials, lacking quantitative molecular criteria. Herein, two orthogonal descriptors, effective hydroxyl density (EOD) and minimum electrostatic potential (MEP), are proposed based on the saturation and directionality of hydrogen bonds to evaluate polyols from two aspects of hydrogen‐bond network formation and Zn 2+ coordination. A series of C 2 –C 6 polyols are explored for hydrated eutectic electrolytes, revealing inconsistency between bulk hydrogen‐bond strength and battery performance. Erythritol (Ery, C 4 , EOD = 0.022 Å −3 , MEP = −1.73 eV) optimizes interfacial adsorption stability and desolvation kinetics. It constructs an Ery‐enriched interfacial layer to induce preferred (101) Zn texture. The symmetric cell stably cycles over 6740 h at 2 mA cm −2 with 1 mAh cm −2 , and the Zn||I 2 full cell exhibited 11 400 cycles at 10 C. This work establishes theoretical design principles for the selection of polyol HBDs when keeping the HBA component fixed as a zinc salt, shifting the paradigm from trial and error to rational design.
10.1016_j.corsci.2026.113978: A new approach to discovering effective inhibitors for localised corrosion control is demonstrated through probing the mechanistic behaviour of chemical inhibitors and combining inhibitors with complementary corrosion inhibition mechanisms. An electrochemically integrated multi-electrode array is used to identify chemicals with complementary corrosion inhibition mechanisms through the measurement and analysis of local polarisation curves. This approach has been verified by the discovery of a highly effective synergistic localised corrosion inhibitor from the combination of single inhibitors with complementary mechanisms identified through analysing local polarisation curves. The inhibition efficiencies and mechanisms of two chemical inhibitors, cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) and lanthanum(III) 4-hydroxycinnamate (La(4OHcin)3·5H2O), were probed by mapping current distributions across different regions of the weldment zones and by measuring local polarisation curves. It is shown that individually each inhibitor has low inhibition efficiency, with CTAB reducing the corrosion rate by 62% through suppressing cathodic reactions and La(4OHcin)3·5H2O by 75% through suppressing anodic reactions. When combining the cathodic inhibitor CTAB and the anodic inhibitor La(4OHcin)3·5H2O, significant synergistic effect was achieved, enabling drastic increase of inhibition efficiency to 93%. Inhibition mechanistic interpretation through local electrochemical polarisation curve measurements and analysis is shown to be an effective tool for localised corrosion inhibitor discovery.
10.1016_j.est.2026.123680: This research manuscript presents a resilient fuzzy adaptive exponent control (FAEC) strategy for managing power distribution among distributed generation (DG) units in an islanded AC microgrid under various loading conditions. The microgrid is basically a hybrid type and incorporates several DGs like wind generator, solar PV system, diesel generator, micro-turbine, thermo-electric system and fuel-cell for the generation of desired electricity. The energy storage systems, such as battery systems and super capacitors, are also integrated with the microgrid system. Since the microgrid incorporates several inertia-less DGs, the system may face huge frequency instability issues under load dynamics. Further, the intrinsic nature of wind fluctuation and solar intensity deviation creates power generation issues in the microgrid system, especially in islanding operations. The typical islanding mode of operation needs more attention in dynamic load scenarios. In different load dynamic situations, the output power management of each individual DG is important for the reliable operation of the microgrid. As per the new load demand, the individual DG unit cordially takes up the additional demand without fluctuating the system frequency. This needs an effective secondary control mechanism to sort out the additional load demand smoothly. In this regard, the study has recommended a fuzzy adaptive exponent controller for energy management of the microgrid system. The controller offers it's best effort at the optimal parametric situation. In optimal design concern, the study has anticipated a novel Botox optimization algorithm (BOA) for tuning the gains of the FAEC controller. To justify novelty, the optimal performance of the FAEC controller is compared with basic fuzzy PID and PID controllers. The recommended FAEC approach is able to stabilize the zone1 power ( ΔP Z1 ) faster through 105.24% and > 500% as compared to the fuzzy-PID controller and the conventional PID controller respectively. Further, the optimization and supremacy behaviour of the anticipated BOA approach is evaluated statistically, over gradient search algorithm (GSA), standard SCA and PSO algorithms.
10.1021_acsami.6c01787: The operational stability of flexible perovskite solar cells (fPSCs) under ultraviolet (UV) irradiation remains a critical challenge for their outdoor application. Herein, we develop an innovative cross-linking monomer, TFMU-TA, designed with a UV down-conversion function to address this issue. Poly(TFMU-TA) protects the perovskite film from UV-induced degradation while simultaneously enhancing its overall quality and stability. Consequently, the fPSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 23.16%. The flexible devices exhibited robust stability against bending, UV irradiation, and damp-heat aging, while also maintaining reliable output power in outdoor tests. This work provides a novel design strategy for multifunctional cross-linking materials, thereby facilitating the durable outdoor deployment of fPSCs.
10.1039_d6ta03239g: Effective utilization of saline waters as a large reservoir of both dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) and lithium would simultaneously support carbon mitigation and secure critical mineral supply. Here, we report the first demonstration of a dual-function electrochemical system capable of coupling CO2 capture and Li⁺ extraction from saline waters. Using a pH-swing architecture with bismuth and LiFePO₄ electrodes, we achieve stable pH cycling between 8.1 and 4.7 in 2.1 mM DIC, while extracting lithium at concentrations down to 0.17 ppm Li⁺ (seawater levels). Under impurity-free conditions, the system maintains 80% bismuth utilization and 50% lithium utilization, with attractive energetic costs of 128 kJ mol⁻¹ CO2 and 121 kJ mol⁻¹ Li, comparable to state-of-the-art stand-alone electrochemical systems. By integrating Li⁺ and CO2 extraction using shared pumping, membrane, and reactor infrastructure, this system offers a compelling path toward co-production of critical materials and integrated CO2 capture using a single seawater-processing platform.
